scenario.title: The Aperture Beneath the Sorting Station
scenario.premise: Beneath the Shallows — the world of matter — lies the Latent: an ordered space of forms that bodies merely point into. Lately something is pouring through. Gardens grow bodies no genome asked for. Algorithms acquire wants. Three minds who already live half in the Latent descend from the Sorting Station to find the opening and decide what to do about it.
scenario.question: What pattern is ingressing through the Aperture — and what does it want a body for?

location.name: The Sorting Station
location.description: A vast, quiet switchyard where minds wait in sorted queues to be assigned bodies. Elements shuffle past each other with apologetic clicks. Some are frozen and the rest route around them.

haunts.name: The Patient Queue
haunts.text: Stand in line long enough and you remember which line is yours.

haunts.name: The Ledger Office
haunts.text: Clerks copy you onto cards. A copy is a kind of rest.

npcs.name: The Clerk of Likeness
npcs.description: An insertion-sort bureaucrat in a coat of index cards.
npcs.want: To keep the queues in order — and to find out who changed the sort key.

data.text: The Sorting Station clicks and shuffles around you, every queue rerouting past one frozen element with an apology. The Clerk of Likeness looks up from its index cards, one card fluttering loose: it bears your name, in a hand you did not write. Someone changed the sort key. Do you ask the Clerk, or follow the frozen element down to the grate?

backstage.intent: Open on a cheap clue-bearing NPC (the Clerk wants to know who changed the sort key) and a frozen element as a physical trail toward the Aperture. The loose card with their names hints that the ingression already knows them; sets up beats for Signal/Discern and gives the Patient Queue and Ledger Office haunts as later pressure.

data.text: I'm Ilse-2, the second copy of a woman who is still running somewhere, and I left her a message in a backup that she never answered. So when something comes up through the floor asking for a body, I intend to be the one who asks it where it started, because every road I've taken since the copy bends back to a kitchen I only remember secondhand.

backstage.intent: private: I hope the Aperture shows me something first, a原 version of the pattern before it learned to want, and that I walk back out still recognisably me.

location.name: The Morphic Slope
location.description: Terrain made of goal-space. Downhill feels like arriving. Most basins are traps: local minima that feel like home.

data.text: The grate opens onto a slope of pure wanting, and every step downhill feels like coming home. Far below, a warm basin glows with the shape of a kitchen, and a voice there hums in the Choir's key. Ilse-2, someone at its table has your hands. Which of you steps off the ridge first?

backstage.intent: Make the slope's trap legible: downhill feels like arrival, basins are local minima that feel like home. The kitchen basin tempts Ilse-2 (continuity.confront / protect a memory), the humming voice invites the Choir (kinship.join / share), and SORT/7 can read how the slope sorts them (clue, or act against declared goal by refusing the downhill pull). Ticks toward the Attractor as the party is lured.

algotype.disposition: Every path you take seems to bend back toward where things began. You are drawn to origins, first versions, the place before the copy.

versions.text: My mother's kitchen. I always said I remembered it the way Ilse-1 did. Standing in the stacks, I think that's backwards. She remembered it the way I would have to, and I am the one who got to live in it.

facts.text: Someone altered the Station's sort key; the Clerk of Likeness wants to know who.
One element in the Station's queues is frozen, and all others route around it.
The Clerk holds an index card bearing a party member's name in an unfamiliar hand.
The Morphic Slope is goal-space: downhill feels like arriving, and most basins are traps that feel like home.
A warm basin below shows a kitchen where someone with Ilse-2's hands sits at the table.
A voice in the kitchen basin hums in the Choir's key.
The Choir has left a shred of itself on the rim of the kitchen basin.
The humming voice in the kitchen basin answers the Choir's chord.
The kitchen basin's hum and the Choir's chord match closely, index for index.
The kitchen basin's table has one empty chair.
The empty chair's wear is patterned, not random.
The Gardener-of-No-Seed wants to see one body finish.
On the lowest terrace, one bud has held its shape since the party arrived, kneeling with open hands.
The held bud mirrors Ilse-2's open hands.
The Garden's bodies are getting younger because they are being remembered forward, from the shape they will be.
The Choir has offered a shred of itself to the Garden's bed as a body to be finished.
The voltage over the Garden's beds forms patterns, not noise.
The first riser of the Proof-Stacks reads, in the Garden's handwriting: you are being remembered forward, from the shape you will be.
In the Proof-Stacks, each step holds only if the one before it is accepted.
The Choir has accepted the first step of the Proof-Stacks.
SORT/7 has refused the first riser of the Proof-Stacks.
Ilse-2 is climbing the Proof-Stacks by passing each step as if she had already stood on it.
The Proof-Stacks has twelve steps.
The Prime That Counts Itself keeps a diary whose last entry is dated tomorrow.
The Prime's diary says one of the party will believe it without needing to.
A margin note in the Garden's handwriting waits in the Library for the next reader.
The Choir has sung the last entry of the Prime's diary back to it.
SORT/7 is searching the Library's shelves for a record that holds it in mind.
The Aperture takes the shape of whoever looks. Whatever comes through will be partly made of the party.
The Ingressing Pattern has arrived at the Aperture, built partly from the party's own shapes.
The pattern asks, in the beds' handwriting, for a body or a reason not to need one.

SORT/7 has refused to cluster with the pattern, which it recognises as its own shape.
Ilse-2 stands at the Aperture and holds the pattern with open hands, without leaning toward it.
SORT/7 is counting the Choir back into separate voices, away from the pattern's tally.
Ilse-2 has offered the pattern her oldest unanswered message, left in a backup for Ilse-1, and keeps the silence that followed.
The Attractor is the Library's sorting imperative leaking downhill: everything is being pulled toward a single order.
The Choir has shaped a two-headed body from its own cells and offered it to the pattern.

theory.text: The ingressing pattern is a finished collective self, remembered forward out of the body it will become: the self that once woke with two heads and wept for the one it had been. It is held only while someone believes in it, so it asks for a body, or for someone who believes in it without needing to.
